text.p: Following are the top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Opposition politician Tang Liang Hong has refused to return to fight libel cases in court because he knows that, under oath, his views on Chinese chauvinism would be exposed, Senior Minister Lee Kuan Yew said.
- Lawyers for Tang Liang Hong found themselves dismissed suddenly by the Woerkers' Party member who had appealed to them on Saturday to continue representing him.
- The fabled Busang gold mine, once described as the richest find this century, is a scam "without precedent in the history of mining", a report has concluded.
- Two CAM International Holdings directors cheated the company and committed criminal breach of trust against it, auditor Eernst & Young alleged.
- Nanyang Press Bhd, the media arm of Malaysia's Hong Leong group, has been approached to buy the Aw family's controlling stake in Hong Kong media group Sing Tao Holdings.
- Communications Minister Mah Bow Tan said implementation of the electronic road-pricing system early next year may cover areas outside the central business district.
- City Developments Ltd has made its first foray innto the Japanese property market, teaming up with Itochu Corporation to buy a commercial building in Osaka for Singapore $91.1 million.
- Transport operator Comfort Group has bought 10 percent of auto parts dealer Tye Soon, which launched its intitial public offering of 59.835 million shares at 31 cents each.
